themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens spiked to 36 this week, a 162% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 13.8 complaints per week, suggesting a possible new venue opening, construction, or enforcement gap affecting residential areas.
evidence: 36 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (162% spike, z-score: 3.86)
Sharp, sudden acceleration suggests new source rather than chronic problem
Concentrated in single week indicates acute trigger—possible new venue, event, or construction
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to identify source: new restaurant/bar opening, construction project, or events at existing venues
Investigate whether new commercial establishments have proper sound permits and noise compliance certifications
Interview residents on when the noise started and whether 311 complaints are being acted on

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints jumped to 4 this week versus a historical average of 0.4 per week, a 967% spike with high statistical significance (z-score: 7.49), indicating a sudden change in park use or activity patterns.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
Extremely sharp statistical anomaly indicates new event, temporary activity, or enforcement change
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for enhanced park safety and security staffing
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to learn what events, activities, or staffing changes occurred in Prospect Park or neighborhood parks this week
Survey residents near major parks (Prospect Park, Carroll Park) about noise sources and timing
Tie to long-standing CB request for park security: are understaffed parks seeing more unmanaged activity?

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Proliferation
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 4 two weeks ago, a 3100% spike from a near-zero baseline (0.1 avg per week), the largest percentage increase among all 311 spikes, suggesting rapid expansion of unlicensed or problematic food vending in the district.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72—highest z-score of all spikes)
Related spike: Vendor Enforcement complaints up 433% last week (4 complaints vs. 0.8 avg), suggesting enforcement is also reactive
Pattern suggests either unlicensed vendors appearing rapidly or existing vendors generating complaints (hygiene, parking, noise)
reporting_angles: Identify which neighborhoods/corners have new or problematic food vendors; map complaint locations
Interview Parks Enforcement and DOH about whether they've noticed an uptick in unlicensed vending or received tips about organized vendor expansion
Talk to established vendors and neighborhood residents about whether the food vendor situation has visibly changed

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related encampment complaints jumped to 9 three weeks ago, a 243% increase over the 8-week baseline of 2.6 per week, correlating with a long-standing community board request for services to address homelessness that has gone unmet year after year.
evidence: 9 encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly baseline (243% spike, z-score: 3.86)
Community board has filed identical budget request for 'services for the homeless' year after year, flagging chronic unmet need
No recent news coverage or constituent escalations in data, suggesting issue may be underreported relative to its severity
reporting_angles: Map where the 9 complaints clustered 3 weeks ago; conduct on-the-ground reporting to assess current encampment status
Interview Parks Enforcement, DHS outreach teams, and local nonprofits about whether encampments grew and whether outreach capacity exists
Investigate why community board's repeated homelessness requests remain unfunded; interview CB members and city budget staff
Profile affected residents and encampment individuals to humanize the crisis

themes_detail.label: Commercial Disposal Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints surged to 3 two weeks ago, a 700% spike from a baseline of 0.4 per week, suggesting emerging issues with restaurant waste management, illegal dumping by businesses, or trash collection enforcement.
evidence: 3 commercial disposal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Coincides with mobile food vendor spike, suggesting possible connection (new vendors = new waste sources)
Aligns with broader pattern of commercial activity spikes (mobile vendors, commercial noise, vendor enforcement)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference commercial disposal complaints with mobile food vendor locations; investigate whether new vendors are creating waste management issues
Contact Sanitation Department to determine whether any new commercial establishments or waste collection route changes occurred 2-3 weeks ago
Inspect complaint locations for visible illegal dumping or overflowing dumpsters
